subject: Request: BYOK + data retention exception for GenHealth pilot
messages:
From: Tim Owens <tim.owens@genhealth.org>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Eve Turner <eve.turner@genhealth.org>; GenHealth Legal <legal@genhealth.org>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Pilot request: BYOK + 180-day retention exception

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team was impressed with the throughput and latency numbers. We're moving to a short internal pilot (POC) for ingesting de-identified patient metadata and a subset of notes. Two asks came out of our security/legal review that we need to confirm before procurement:

1) BYOK: GenHealth requires a customer-managed key for the pilot environment (we can provide a KMS policy and key material). Can Redwood support a temporary BYOK bound to a private deployment/workload for the pilot?

2) Retention exception: standard Redwood retention is 30 days for PII-derived tokens. For the pilot they need a 180-day retention window for auditability. They're asking what controls and mitigations you require to approve such an exception (access controls, audit logs, key escrow, deletion tickets).

I'll attach the brief questionnaire GenHealth completed and our legal team's list of requested controls. We're aiming to sign the PO by end of next week if these are feasible. Can you loop in the right folks and confirm feasibility + any blocking product/ops work?

Tim
Tim Owens
IT Security, GenHealth
-- attachment: genhealth_pci_questionnaire.pdf (17 KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 18:34:00 -0000
Subject: Fwd: Pilot request: BYOK + 180-day retention exception

Looping you in — GenHealth is asking for a temporary BYOK for the pilot plus a retention exception to 180 days. Key points: they expect to provide KMS artifacts and want clear controls for approving the retention extension.

Can Product (Marissa) and Security/Compliance (Rishi, Neha) weigh in on:
- Feasibility for a short-term BYOK on a private/dedicated pilot and estimated ops work (key wrapping, rotation policy, key lifecycle).
- Minimum controls to approve 180-day retention (role-based access, audit log retention, deletion playbook, attestation cadence).
- Any legal/regulatory red flags for accepting patient metadata even if de-identified.

I suggested we treat this as an "exception-bound-by-contract" (i.e., on-boarding paperwork + timeboxed commitment). We need an answer by EOD Thurs to hit the PO timeline.

--Kimberly
kimberly park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:06:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot request: BYOK + 180-day retention exception

Thanks for the ping. Quick notes from Product POV after a fast sync with infra:

- BYOK: We can support a pilot-level BYOK if the customer deploys to Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with a reserved pool. For a hosted tenant this is not supported today. Work: we need a one-off onboarding runbook (tech + ops) and an automated key import path to avoid manual HSM ops. Est. effort: 3-4 engineering days + 1 ops day to validate.

- Retention 180d: We're conservative for PII-derived artifacts in hosted mode, but for Private/Dedicated we can allow 180d as a contract-bound exception given:
  * Explicit contract clause limiting scope (pilot only)
  * Access controls: RBAC tied to customer-specific principals, no cross-tenant admin rights
  * Audit logs: make sure we retain and export audit logs to a customer-provided S3 for independent archival (or keep a signed hash)

Open question: do we require an automated rollback to 30d after the pilot or will legal sign the timebox into the contract? I prefer automatic enforcement.

I'll draft a short "pilot controls" checklist and Ops runbook stub — assigning Rishi and Neha to fill compliance/crypto specifics.

Marissa
Senior PM, Redwood Inference
-- attachment: proposed-mop-2027-04-21.docx (12 KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Pilot request: BYOK + 180-day retention exception

Agree with Marissa. Compliance notes from my side:

- BYOK: We need a defined KMS policy template and an HSM import checklist. We must validate key origin and provide audit evidence for key import events (who/when). No key escrow by Redwood unless contractually required; if GenHealth insists on escrow we need legal + vault ops sign-off.

- Retention: To approve 180-day retention on de-identified data we need:
  1) A documented de-identification procedure (data elements removed/hashed) and a small sample validation run by CS.
  2) RBAC mapped to customer principals with MFA enforced for any role that can view raw inputs.
  3) Signed access attestation quarterly for the pilot duration.
  4) Exportable audit logs: we can push a copy to their S3 or a signed append-only log (we have a prototype auditstream).

- Operational gating: Ops must be able to flip retention back to 30d automatically. I'll ask infra to add a retention flag in the tenant config that can be toggled and audited.

I'll prepare the compliance checklist and a minimal acceptance criteria doc by tomorrow noon.

Rishi
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Owens <tim.owens@genhealth.org>, Eve Turner <eve.turner@genhealth.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Pilot request: BYOK + 180-day retention exception

Tim — quick update and next steps:

1) Feasibility: Redwood can support a BYOK-bound pilot if GenHealth runs the pilot on Redwood Private or a Dedicated reserved pool. We will not support BYOK on hosted shared tenants.

2) Retention: We can approve a 180-day retention as a contract-scoped exception for the pilot provided GenHealth signs the pilot controls addendum (timebox + attestation + exportable audit logs). Redwood will implement an automatic rollback to 30 days at pilot end unless Legal signs an extension.

3) Timeline & ops: Estimated non-blocking effort: 4 engineering days + 1 ops day for BYOK onboarding and retention flag. Compliance will produce a checklist tomorrow.

Ask: Can you confirm (a) which deployment option you want (Private vs Dedicated), (b) a primary legal point of contact for the addendum, and (c) whether GenHealth prefers audit logs pushed to their S3 or a signed log export? Once we have that we'll send a draft addendum and an onboarding MOP.

Thanks — aiming to have the addendum and MOP ready for signature within 3 business days once deployment choice is confirmed.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
